data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The dilemma is a category error arising from applying Bayesian/justificationist standards to a falsificationist framework; the preference is defensible as a 'conventionalist' decision to treat the best-tested theory as the working hypothesis, costing us the comfort of believing it is 'probably' true.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If scientists cannot psychologically separate 'acting on' from 'believing in' a theory.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the 'convention' itself requires an inductive justification to be adopted rationally.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the 'cost' of radical fallibilism undermines the motivation to conduct science at all.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Popper's system operates on a different logic where 'rationality' means 'openness to criticism,' not 'maximization of probability.'
